To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the corticostriatocortical loop is a disclosed loop, with a closed loop (operative) component that is open to input from a wider range of cortical sources (contextual).

the cortico-basalganglia (BG) loop, thought to underlie momentary action selection, is a closed circuit that opens to outside influence at its cortical input, which we term the operative input, and which is the basis of a new model of the BG loop, which we term disclosed loop.

the cortico-basalganglia-thalamocortical circuit is a disclosed loop, with a mandatory component of unidirectional input from cortex, which we call operative, and a broader component, contextual, which converges upon the same target.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional logic of cortico-striato-thalamocortical circuitry.
the logic of corticofugal connections, which is a fundamental aspect of brain function.
the functional organisation of corticostripatal connections, and the cortico-Basal Ganglia (BG) loop, and how these contribute to the control of movement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cortico-BGs loop is a disclosed loop, in which operative input is the initial step, and in which a broad set of contextual inputs, converging from a range of cortical sources, determine the balance of direct and indirect activity.
, although corticostriato-BG circuitry is complex, its functional logic is simple, in that it implements an elegant and powerful algorithm for action selection.
the disclosed loop is a functional logic for corticostriatum that is consistent with all available data, and provides a coherent framework within which to integrate new data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cortico-BGT circuitry is designed for action selection, and that this is a process in which both the positive and negative aspects of action are simultaneously considered.
the cortico-BGs are a distributed network of parallel loops, each of which has the potential to initiate and control a distinct motor act.
the disclosed loop is the functional unit of corticostrial connectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the striatum is not a passive relay, but rather an active participant in the cortico-BGT loop, and that its function is to provide a mechanism of action selection that is sensitive to the current state and context of action.
the cortico-BGs are a closed circuit with open access to external influences.
, in order to understand the corticostriatum and BG loop, we should focus on the functional logic of the corticostrial input, and the ensuing SPN responses.
